title: The canonical Proj map identifies an affine principal chart
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an invertible module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], put $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, and for homogeneous $s\in S$ of positive degree write $X_s$ for its nonvanishing open. Assume every point of $X$ lies in some such $X_s$. Then there exists a canonical morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj], and for every positive-degree homogeneous $s\in S$ one has $f^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$. If $\mathcal L$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] and $X_s$ is affine, then the induced morphism $X_s\to D_+(s)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), existence of the canonical morphism under the positive-degree homogeneous cover hypothesis; Properties Lemma 01Q1 (lemma-ample-immersion-into-proj), proof of the inverse-image identity and localization isomorphism via Lemma 01PW

proof.text: The section-ring construction in [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map] applies because the positive-degree homogeneous nonvanishing opens cover $X$; it supplies the canonical morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ and the identity $f^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$ for every such $s$.

By the definition of ampleness [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $X$ is quasi-compact. The same ampleness hypothesis gives that $X$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated], and hence quasi-separated (a separated morphism has quasi-compact diagonal).

Fix a positive-degree homogeneous $s\in S$ of degree $d>0$ with $X_s$ affine. Regard $s$ as a degree-one section of the invertible module $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$. Applying [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology] with $p=0$, $F=\mathcal O_X$, and $\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ gives an isomorphism $\Gamma_*(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})_{(s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_X)$ sending $\xi/s^n$ to $s^{-n}\xi$. The degree-zero part of the localization of the Veronese section ring $\Gamma_*(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ at $s$ is the same ring $S_{(s)}$ (elementary reindexing of degrees), so this is $S_{(s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 09MR (p=0, applied to the Veronese module)

proof.text: By [def-pc-proj], $D_+(s)=\operatorname{Spec}(S_{(s)})$. By the additional clause of [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map], the ring map induced by $f|_{X_s}:X_s\to D_+(s)$ is exactly $S_{(s)}\to\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_X)$, $\xi/s^n\mapsto s^{-n}\xi$; hence it is an isomorphism by step 3.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01Q1, localization paragraph; Lemma 01PZ (3) and Constructions Lemma 01N8

proof.text: Both $X_s$ and $D_+(s)$ are affine, and their induced map on global sections is an isomorphism by step 3. Therefore $f|_{X_s}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-affine-global-sections-iso].
